The implementation plan is ready for approval:

- [Implementation plan](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/plan.md)
- [Technical research](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/research.md)
- [Data model](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/data-model.md)
- [API contract](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/contracts/openapi.yaml)
- [UI behavior contract](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/contracts/ui-behavior.md)
- [Validation guide](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/quickstart.md)

The automatic-title behavior is explicit: pasting a valid link starts retrieval automatically, requires no extra button, remains editable, and never overwrites a title the user types while retrieval is pending.

The design uses a React/TypeScript client, Node/Express service, and SQLite. Title retrieval includes OWASP-aligned protections against private-network access, unsafe redirects, DNS pinning, oversized responses, and timeouts. [OWASP guidance](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Server_Side_Request_Forgery_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html)

Branch reference: `001-manage-bookmarks`. No tasks or application code have been generated yet. Please approve the plan or request changes; approval unlocks task generation.

The plan works for me. The automatic-title part is exactly what I asked about — pasting a link starts finding the title on its own, I can still edit it, and it won't stomp on a title I've typed myself. I also like that saving isn't held up if the title lookup is slow or fails.

The rest lines up with what I want too: browsing newest-first, searching across titles/addresses/notes/tags, filtering by tags and favorites, editing, archiving and restoring, and a confirmation before anything is permanently deleted.

content:
The bookmark manager is built and ready for review at:

**http://maker:4000/**

Completed functionality includes:

- Automatic title suggestions immediately after pasting or leaving a URL
- Editable titles with protection against overwriting manual input
- Graceful manual fallback when title retrieval fails
- Newest-first browsing, search, tags, favorites, and combined filters
- Duplicate-link warnings with explicit continuation
- Editing, archiving, restoring, and confirmed permanent deletion
- Private accounts and owner-isolated collections
- Responsive desktop/mobile interface

Validation passed:

- 48/48 implementation tasks complete
- 25 unit, contract, integration, security, and performance tests
- 5 Playwright browser journeys
- Formatting, linting, strict type checking, and production build
- Real external title retrieval verified with “Example Domain”
- 10,000-bookmark search comfortably within the one-second target

Key files: [README](/work/README.md), [completed tasks](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/tasks.md), and [application source](/work/src/client/App.tsx).

I went through it myself and the important things all work: pasting a link pulls in the title automatically ("Example Domain" came back on its own), saving with tags and notes works, trying to save the same link again warns me and points to the one I already have, searching finds the right bookmark and shows nothing for a term that doesn't match, and I can archive an item out of my main list, find it in the archived view, restore it, and permanently delete it. That's exactly what I wanted — one place to save links and keep them organized.

This does everything I set out to do. I'm happy with it.
